![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/61bd212879bc2f37dba7637bb3b126e33c5f7b0fbebd5a676874d9b3f6bc38da.png)

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=6y$ for $x\ge 0,$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $3$ centered at $(0,3,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=6y$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =6y \\ {\rho }^{2} & =6\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho -6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/f52fe1c2e73dcbe972d72d263a5a43f2c99dbd573395fbf6e3a3b78b46e1f461.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{1}{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}[\rho ]_{\rho =0}^{\rho =6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}(6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-0)\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{\pi }dϕ\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,d\theta  \\  & =6[ϕ]_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi }\cdot [-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ]_{\theta =0}^{\theta =\pi /2} \\  & =6(\pi -0)\cdot (-0+1) \\  & =6\pi \end{aligned}
$$
